notes: Total 18 = hard. The pipeline is a long chain of dependent stages that must stay mutually consistent: learn a BPE tokenizer (vocab + merge rules in the loader's exact formats), train a 300-dim word2vec-style embedding matrix whose rows exactly equal the vocab and are distributionally meaningful (verified by within-class vs cross-class cosine separation on frequently co-occurring anchors), build a fasttext-style linear classifier over mean-pooled word embeddings that clears a holdout-accuracy floor while its serialized model stays under a size budget, emit a per-model metrics table (model, correlation, error, penalty, dof) with internally consistent values, and serialize a Vocab dataclass whose word<->index maps are exact inverses sized to the embedding rows. Difficulty comes from coordinating tokenizer/embedding/classifier/metadata so every invariant holds simultaneously, generalising the whole runner to fresh and malformed synthetic corpora (blank, punctuation-only, digit-only, short, duplicate, and missing-TAB rows), and respecting the accuracy-vs-size budget and verifier time budget. Leaning implementation: a gensim+scikit-learn rapid pipeline stands in for the classic C++ fasttext binary (no compiled-toolchain step), but every competency is genuinely exercised for real.
